text: Key conventions brief: Naming: air_ prefix high-level user functions; at_ prefix raw API wrappers (exported, documented advanced). Token parameter: .token (dotted) air_* — signals optional, project-level. token (undotted) at_* — callers API-knowledgeable may supply tokens explicitly. Argument ordering: -default args first, defaulted args second, project-level args last. piped main object goes first. ID hierarchy: record → field → base → workspace. Pipe: base R |> throughout (requires R >= 4.1.0). Error handling: cli_abort(), cli_warn(), cli_inform() cli/rlang. Never use base stop(), warning(), message(). cli pluralization: use {.val {n} field{?s}} syntax (count variable like {n_fields} field{?s}). use {?s} alone unknown-length vector — always bind count. Mocking: local_mocked_bindings() preferred httptest2 new tests, especially write operations. Batch size: 10 records per API call (Airtable hard limit). Typecast default: TRUE high-level air_* ops; FALSE low-level at_* ops. air_ vs at_ prefixes? two layers different stability contracts. at_* functions thin wrappers whose signatures track Airtable REST API closely — callers use accept API can change. air_* functions present stable, ergonomic interface; internals can change API evolves. distinct prefixes makes contract visible tab-completion. .token (dotted) air_* functions? Dotted arguments hidden tab-completion R IDEs, keeps primary interface clean. users set token via AIRTABLE_API_KEY options(airtable2.token = ...) never think . dotted convention signals “secondary concern callers.” Low-level at_* callers API-knowledgeable may legitimately want pass tokens explicitly, token (undotted) appropriate . httr2 instead httr? httr2 provides built-req_retry() req_throttle(), making retry rate-limit logic declarative rather manual. also makes requests composable (step returns modified request object) testable. DBI layer? DBI interface enables standard R database workflows (dbReadTable(), dbWriteTable()) gives Positron/RStudio connection pane integration free. also makes airtable2 interoperable package knows talk DBI connections. DBI layer wraps air_* functions — adds new API calls, just adapts interface. Auth resolution order: arg → option → env var standard R pattern used usethis, gh, similar packages. option layer (getOption("airtable2.token")) lets users set session default programmatically without touching environment. env var layer (AIRTABLE_API_KEY) works .Renviron, CI, Docker, similar contexts. native pipe |> magrittr %>%? Fewer dependencies, faster loading, R >= 4.1.0 already required reasons. native pipe covers patterns used package. dbplyr/SQL translation? Airtable relational database. query language filterByFormula, custom formula language. Building full SQL--formula translator fragile incomplete. Users need filtering pass formula = air_read() directly. Arg ordering rationale Consistent arg ordering reduces cognitive load. -default args first means function can always called positionally. Project-level args (.token, .base_id) last means disappear tab-completion near front signature. ID hierarchy (record → field → base → workspace) follows Airtable containment hierarchy. Record matching upsert/sync airtable_id present data, used direct record updates (efficient). Records without airtable_id fall back merge_on field matching. paths must work, can mixed within single call.

code: updated <- data.frame(   Name = c("Zara Okonkwo", "Dmitri Volkov", "New Collaborator"),   Age = c(35L, 42L, 27L) )  result <- air_upsert(   updated,   "Artists",   merge_on = "Name",   base_id = demo_base_id ) # Upsert complete: 1 created, 2 updated. result$created # record IDs of new records result$updated # record IDs of updated records desired <- data.frame(   Name = c("Zara Okonkwo", "Dmitri Volkov"),   Age = c(35L, 42L) )  result <- air_sync(   desired,   "Artists",   key = "Name",   base_id = demo_base_id,   delete_missing = TRUE ) # Sync complete: 0 created, 2 updated, 13 deleted, 0 unchanged.

title: Using airtable2 with DBI
text: airtable2 provides DBI interface can use familiar DBI::dbConnect(), DBI::dbReadTable(), DBI::dbWriteTable(), related functions interact Airtable bases. makes easy integrate Airtable existing R workflows expect standard database connections, enables RStudio Positron connection pane point--click table browsing. text: air_meta_sync() takes documentation one step . recommended workflow: Call air_meta_init() create _metadata table base, populated current schema. Open base Airtable edit description text directly _metadata table — R required. title: Metadata, Schema, and Backup in airtable2
text: following end--end example covers typical backup--migrate scenario. chunks use eval = FALSE require live API credentials.
code: library(airtable2)  # Step 1: Dump the source base to a local directory air_dump(   "appSOURCEBASE",   dir     = "backup/",   format  = "json",   attachments = "file"   # download all attachment files ) # Step 2: Inspect the schema to identify computed fields schema <- jsonlite::read_json("backup/schema.json")  # Or use air_schema() on the live base schema_tbl <- air_schema("appSOURCEBASE") computed_types <- c(   "formula", "rollup", "lookup", "count", "autoNumber",   "createdTime", "lastModifiedTime", "createdBy", "lastModifiedBy" ) needs_manual <- lapply(schema_tbl$fields, function(f) {   f[f$type %in% computed_types, c("name", "type")] }) names(needs_manual) <- schema_tbl$table_name needs_manual # Step 3: Restore to a new base in the same (or different) workspace new_id <- air_restore(   "backup/",   base_name    = "Projects (migrated)",   workspace_id = "wspTARGETWORKSPACE" ) # Step 4: Verify record counts match original <- air_schema("appSOURCEBASE") restored  <- air_schema(new_id)  # Check table names setdiff(original$table_name, restored$table_name)  # Should be character(0) # Step 5 (manual): In the Airtable UI, re-create computed fields # (formulas, rollups, lookups, autoNumber, etc.) in the new base. # Use the saved schema.json as a reference.  # Step 6: Re-link records if any tables use multipleRecordLinks # (see the next section)

title: Metadata, Schema, and Backup in airtable2
text: base restored, every record receives new Airtable record ID. air_restore() handles automatically: default (restore_linked_fields = TRUE), records created runs two-step pass: Field definitions — multipleRecordLinks fields recreated linkedTableId remapped new base’s table IDs. Cell values — link values dump (old record IDs) remapped new record IDs using insertion-order mapping, written back via air_upsert(). automatic re-linking might sufficient: automatic approach matches records insertion order, works dump restore done unit. merging records multiple sources, tables partially restored, may need re-link manually using natural key:
code: # Full restore — linked-record fields AND cell values restored automatically new_base_id <- air_restore(   "backup/",   workspace_id = Sys.getenv("AIRTABLE_WORKSPACE_ID"),   base_name = "Restored Base" ) # Creating base "Restored Base"... # Adding fields... # Inserting records... # Recreated 2 link fields and 0 dependent fields. # Re-linked records in 1 table. # Restore complete. New base ID: appYYYYYYYY.  # Skip the re-linking step (faster; links will be empty) new_base_id <- air_restore(   "backup/",   workspace_id = Sys.getenv("AIRTABLE_WORKSPACE_ID"),   restore_linked_fields = FALSE ) # Manual re-link using a stable natural key (e.g. Name/Email) # Useful when insertion order doesn't reliably map old IDs to new ones. projects_new <- air_read("Projects", new_base_id) artists_new  <- air_read("Artists",  new_base_id)  # Build old-to-new ID map using Name as stable key # (assumes artists_old was saved from the source base before restore) id_map <- stats::setNames(artists_new$airtable_id, artists_old$Name) remap  <- function(ids) lapply(ids, function(v) unname(id_map[v]))  projects_new$`Lead Artist` <- remap(projects_new$`Lead Artist`) air_upsert(   projects_new[, c("airtable_id", "Lead Artist")],   "Projects",   merge_on = "airtable_id",   base_id = new_base_id )

title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: Airtable’s Attachments field holds one files per record. read, cell list attachment objects, minimum: filename — original file name url — temporary Airtable-hosted download URL size — file size bytes type — MIME type airtable2 wraps air_attachments list-column. Important: Airtable attachment URLs temporary expire short time (typically hours). Always re-fetch records downloading significant time passed since last air_read() call. att[] tag marks column air_attachments. single attachment shows filename; multiple attachments show first_file.ext +N; empty field NA. Inspect single row’s attachment metadata directly:
code: projects <- air_read("appXXXXXX", "Projects") projects #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   airtable_id  name    docs #>   <chr>        <chr>   <att[]> #> 1 recAAAAAAAA  Alpha   brief.pdf #> 2 recBBBBBBBB  Beta    report.docx +1 #> 3 recCCCCCCCC  Gamma   NA projects$docs[[2]] #> [[1]] #> [[1]]$id #> [1] "attXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" #> [[1]]$filename #> [1] "report.docx" #> [[1]]$url #> [1] "https://dl.airtable.com/..." #> [[1]]$size #> [1] 42816 #> [[1]]$type #> [1] "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" #> #> [[2]] #> [[2]]$filename #> [1] "notes.txt" #> ...

title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: air_read_attachments() fetches attachments given field returns flat tibble one row per file. dest argument controls output format: "meta" — valid value ; air_read_attachments() always downloads content. Use air_flatten_attachments() list-column need metadata. "blob" — download files raw byte vectors stored blob list-column "file" — write files disk dir/; returns local_path column can also control attachment mode directly air_read() using attachments argument. downloads files part initial read augments attachment objects list-column content (blob) local_path (file) field:
code: # Download as raw bytes (in-memory) blobs <- air_read_attachments(   base_id = "appXXXXXX",   table = "Projects",   field = "docs",   dest = "blob" ) blobs #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   airtable_id  filename       url                    size    type           blob #>   <chr>        <chr>          <chr>                 <int>    <chr>          <list> #> 1 recAAAAAAAA  brief.pdf      https://dl.airtable…  18432    application/… <raw[18432]> #> 2 recBBBBBBBB  report.docx    https://dl.airtable…  42816    application/… <raw[42816]> #> 3 recBBBBBBBB  notes.txt      https://dl.airtable…   1024    text/plain    <raw[1024]> # Save files to disk: one sub-directory per record files <- air_read_attachments(   base_id = "appXXXXXX",   table = "Projects",   field = "docs",   dest = "file",   dir = "downloads/" ) files #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   airtable_id  filename     url                  size  type          local_path #>   <chr>        <chr>        <chr>               <int>  <chr>         <chr> #> 1 recAAAAAAAA  brief.pdf    https://…           18432  application/… downloads/brief.pdf #> 2 recBBBBBBBB  report.docx  https://…           42816  application/… downloads/report.docx #> 3 recBBBBBBBB  notes.txt    https://…            1024  text/plain    downloads/notes.txt # Download attachments to disk while reading projects <- air_read(   "appXXXXXX",   "Projects",   attachments = "file",   attachment_dir = "downloads/" ) # Now each attachment object in projects$docs has a $local_path entry projects$docs[[1]][[1]]$local_path #> [1] "downloads/recAAAAAAAA/brief.pdf"

what: Stable preview URLs and the temporary-URL caveat
title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: url field attachment object temporary: Airtable generates signed airtableusercontent.com URL expires approximately two hours API call. Never save URL database share permanent link — stop working shortly fetch . function air_attachment_preview_url() always returns NA_character_. intentional correct. Airtable expose stable viewer URLs REST API. stable URL — one hosted airtable.com rather airtableusercontent.com — can obtained opening attachment Airtable web app copying address bar URL. Workaround stable link: navigate record Airtable web app, click attachment thumbnail open viewer, copy URL browser’s address bar. URL originates airtable.com expire.
code: # The url field in each attachment expires after ~2 hours: projects$Files[[1]][[1]]$url #> [1] "https://v5.airtableusercontent.com/v3/..."  # <- expires soon  # air_attachment_preview_url() always returns NA — this is correct behaviour: air_attachment_preview_url(projects$Files[[1]][[1]]) #> [1] NA #> i Airtable does not expose stable viewer URLs through the REST API. #> i To get a permanent shareable link: open the record in the Airtable web app, #>   click the attachment, and copy the URL from your browser's address bar. #>   That URL (from airtable.com) does not expire.

title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: Airtable two collaborator field types: Collaborator (collaborator) — single workspace member. Also used built-Created Last modified fields. Multiple collaborators (multipleCollaborators) — zero workspace members. collaborator object three fields: id (Airtable user ID), email, name. Single-collaborator fields become air_collaborator list-column (type tag collab). Multi-collaborator fields become air_collaborators list-column (type tag collabs).
code: tasks <- air_read("appXXXXXX", "Tasks") tasks #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   airtable_id  title         assigned_to            reviewers #>   <chr>        <chr>         <collab>               <collabs> #> 1 recAAAAAAAA  Write tests   Alice <alice@co.com>   Bob <bob@co.com> #> 2 recBBBBBBBB  Review PR     Bob <bob@co.com>       Alice <alice@co.com> +1 #> 3 recCCCCCCCC  Deploy        NA                     NA # Single collaborator: a named list tasks$assigned_to[[1]] #> $id #> [1] "usrXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" #> $email #> [1] "alice@co.com" #> $name #> [1] "Alice"

title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: air_simplify() processes every list-column tibble , converting simplest character representation using appropriate type-specific flattener. quickest way get fully flat, -atomic data frame export display: schema available (passed schema argument), air_simplify() uses field type pick right flattener. Without schema, falls back generic paste(format(v), collapse = ", ") list element.
code: projects <- air_read("appXXXXXX", "Projects")  # Before: list-columns with air_* classes str(projects$tags) #>  air_multiselect [1:4] ...  flat <- air_simplify(projects) flat #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   airtable_id  name    tags                owner_ids #>   <chr>        <chr>   <chr>               <chr> #> 1 recAAAAAAAA  Alpha   R, data, analysis   recPPPPPPPP #> 2 recBBBBBBBB  Beta    data                recQQQQQQQQ, recRRRRRRRR #> 3 recCCCCCCCC  Gamma   NA                  NA #> 4 recDDDDDDDD  Delta   R, reporting        NA  # After: plain character columns str(flat$tags) #>  chr [1:4] "R, data, analysis" "data" NA "R, reporting" # at_get_schema() returns all tables; find the one named "Projects" all_tables <- at_get_schema("appXXXXXX") projects_table <- Filter(function(t) t$name == "Projects", all_tables)[[1]] schema <- projects_table$fields flat <- air_simplify(projects, schema = schema)

what: When to use air_simplify() vs. the type-specific flatteners
title: Special Field Types in airtable2
text: Use air_simplify() want quick flat snapshot whole table, e.g., export CSV inspect data interactively. Use type-specific flatteners (air_flatten_multiselect(), air_flatten_links(), air_flatten_attachments(), air_flatten_collaborator()) need control delimiters, output format, want work individual columns pipeline. Avoid air_simplify() writing data back Airtable. original air_* list-columns round-trip correctly; flattened strings (need air_expand_multiselect() etc. convert back).

title: airtable2 0.0.0.9000
text: Attachment uploads now work. at_upload_attachment() (air_write_attachments() / air_sync_attachments() / air_demo() paths call ) previously POSTed api.airtable.com always got 404, Airtable serves uploadAttachment endpoint separate host. Uploads now go content.airtable.com. air_req() gained host argument select host. API errors now informative: air_perform() surfaces Airtable’s error type message plus actionable hints (e.g. wrong table name / missing permission, unknown field name, invalid filterByFormula). also fixes dead error handler — old code caught non-existent httr2_http_error condition class, Airtable’s explanation silently dropped users saw bare HTTP status. air_api_usage() now counts parallel attachment downloads (previously bypassed counter via req_perform_parallel()), print method shows workspace ID clickable link. Airtable IDs air_browse() messages now clickable cli hyperlinks. air_browse() now honors base_id/table_id arguments (previously leaked utils::browseURL()), browsing table/view ID works. .onAttach now warns (, via packageStartupMessage()) airtabler airtable2 loaded function names mask. Fixed pkgdown reference index site builds (documented AirtableDriver topic; indexed air_req()/air_token() package doc).
